entries.example: All his possessions were destroyed in the terrible fire. [everything he owned]
Don't leave any of your belongings here; we've had a few thefts recently. [smaller things, e.g. bag, camera, coat; always plural]

entries.def: in the singular can mean a big area of private land and the buildings on it, or all of someone's wealth upon death
entries.example: She owns a huge estate in Scotland. [land, etc.]
After his death, his estate was calculated at £3 million. [all his wealth]

entries.def: (uncountable) is used in a general sense for houses, land, etc.
entries.example: He's only fourteen; he's too young to own property.

entries.def: (countable) is a building (e.g. house, office-block) or land
entries.example: She owns some valuable properties in the town-centre.

entries.def: [formal; used for shops, businesses etc.; owner is less formal]
entries.example: The proprietor of this restaurant is a friend of mine.
entries.group: Words for people connected with ownership

entries.example: The landlord/lady has put the rent up.
entries.group: Words for people connected with ownership

entries.example: Do you own this house? No we're just tenants.

entries.def: [rent and hire are both commonly used]

entries.def: when you lend, you give, when you borrow, you receive
entries.example: That tape-recorder you lent me last week, could I borrow it again?
I'm trying to get a loan from the bank to buy a boat.
